- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment shift.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting downward; apply early correction if sentiment >0 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 3σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day from day 5 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1–2 negative, then 1–2 positive), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
